I'm 2 or 3 weeks into it now, with about 120 dwellers. I haven't paid any real money thus far. I think as far as these mobile resource management games go, it's one of the better ones. In most of them you're managing a single resource - in-game money - and as long as you have enough of it, there's no problem you can't solve. Tiny Death Star was bad about that - it was basically just 'do things to make money to build rooms to do things to make money to build rooms'. This one has an interesting rock-paper-scissors balance between resources - if you're low on food, for instance, you need more food rooms (necessitating money to build and power to run), and people to work them (necessitating living space, water, and food itself). Striking a balance while expanding can be fun, and keeping everyone fed during the several days it takes to train a new generation can be challenging.

I do think a lot of the more complex mechanics aren't explained very well, though, which can lead to frustration. For instance, everyone I've known had a point in their vault where everyone kept getting radiation sickness, and they couldn't figure out why (dwellers ran out of clean water). Or had a molerat attack that wiped out most of the vault (almost everyone in your vault should train until they have nearly-capped strength, luck, and endurance - base SPECIAL stats are often more important than level or equipment).
